dbError.title: The local database could not be opened
dbError.body: Pharos has not modified any file. Close the app and try again; if it keeps happening, share this detail with support.
dbError.inUseTitle: Another Pharos is updating your data
dbError.inUseBody: Another Pharos window or the Pharos CLI is updating this computer’s database (for example, after installing a new version). Wait until it finishes and press “Try again”. No file has been modified.
dbError.noSpaceTitle: Not enough space to update your data
dbError.noSpaceBody: To convert it safely, Pharos needs room for a backup and for the new database. Your data has not been touched. Free up disk space (how much is shown below) and try again.
dbError.convertFailedTitle: Your data could not be updated
dbError.convertFailedBody: Your data is intact: the original file was not modified and there is a backup. You can try again; if it fails again, export the diagnostics from Help and send them (they contain neither your data nor your key).
dbError.missingBody: Your data moved to pharos.db, which is not in the data folder. Put it back there (or a pharos.db.bak-… copy) and open Pharos again. Pharos does not create an empty database in its place.
dbError.convertingTitle: Updating the format of your data
dbError.convertingBody: This happens once, in this version. From now on, Pharos saves every change instantly.
dbError.convertingKeepOpen: Do not close Pharos. If it closes, it picks up where it left off next time.
dbError.newerTitle: This data comes from a newer version of Pharos
dbError.newerBody: The local database was saved by a more recent version than this one. To avoid damaging it, Pharos neither opens nor modifies it. Install that version or a later one.
dbError.keyMissingTitle: The local database key is missing
dbError.keyMismatchTitle: The stored key does not open the local database
dbError.keyBody: Your data is still encrypted on this computer, but its key is not in the system credential store (this happens on a new PC or after reinstalling Windows). Enter the recovery key you saved in Administration › Security to open it. Pharos changes no file until the key is right.

evidence.desktopOnly: Evidence is stored encrypted on this device: its usage and verification are only in the desktop app.

usage.title: Evidence store
usage.desc: Attachments are stored encrypted in the evidence folder, next to the database. They sync with your workspace: each file is uploaded once and the other devices download it after syncing. Those of a manual run in progress wait until you save the result.
usage.byOwnerHint: Only current attachments: deleted and expired ones are not counted.
usage.expiredHint: Their content was deleted when it expired; the record that they existed is kept.
usage.rawReportsHint: Imported reports (JUnit, Allure…) are deleted when they expire; the results read from them stay.
usage.totalHint: Only the files on this device: missing ones are not counted. Identical content is stored once, so one file can serve several attachments (for example, a defect created from a result uses that result's evidence).
usage.failed: The evidence store could not be read: {{reason}}
usage.markedHint: Kept across restarts. Press «Verify evidence» to see where they are used.

retention.title: Retention per project
retention.desc: How long each kind of evidence of a project is kept before its file expires. Expiring removes the file, never the result: the record that it existed stays.
retention.deviceOnly: This setting is for this device only: it does not sync. Each device expires its own copies, at startup and after each sync.
retention.exceptionsText: The evidence of manual execution, of a final failed or blocked result, and of a result linked to an open defect. Planner, defect and draft attachments never expire either.
retention.pending: To save: {{changes}}. Press “Save” to apply the changes.
retention.failed: The retention could not be read or saved.
retention.confirmMessage: With the new period, the next pass (at startup or after a sync) removes these files from this device. The results stay; the files cannot be recovered.
retention.daysInvalid: Enter a number of days from 1 to {{max}}.

check.title: Verify evidence
check.desc: Checks that every file is there and decrypts, and looks for files no row knows. It never deletes anything by itself.
check.actionHint: It reads and decrypts every file, so it may take a while with a lot of evidence. You can keep working meanwhile.
check.busy: A verification or a repair is already running.
check.failed: The evidence could not be verified: {{reason}}
check.cancelled: Verification cancelled: {{done}} of {{total}} files were checked. What was checked is marked; verify again for the rest.

orphans.title: Files without a record ({{count}})
orphans.desc: No row of this database knows them. They may belong to a database moved aside or restored, or to another instance: delete them only if you know they are not needed.
orphans.recentHint: Created or modified in the last 24 hours (a copy or a restore counts as new): it cannot be deleted.
orphans.confirmMessage: They are deleted from disk and cannot be recovered. If they belong to a database moved aside, that database loses those attachments. Files created or modified in the last 24 hours and, on Windows only, files another program has open are skipped. If another Pharos window uses this same data folder, close it first.

users.lastAdmin: There must be at least one administrator.

stepDesc.identification: The document’s identification block (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3): title, status, version, date and author. It is shown on the PDF’s cover.
stepDesc.summary: A short introduction: what is tested and why.
stepDesc.scope: What is in and out of the testing.
stepDesc.levelsTypes: What is tested, at which level and with which type (ISTQB). Levels say where it is tested: a component, its interfaces, the whole system end to end, or the user’s and business’s acceptance. Types say which characteristic is checked: functional, non-functional (performance, security…) or confirmation and regression after a change. Tick at least one level and one type; you can add your own types.
stepDesc.methodology: How the testing work is organised.
stepDesc.deliverables: Documents and artefacts the test team produces. Tick what will be delivered when the cycle closes; the list follows the ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 documentation. Deliverables you add go to “Own” and are removed with ✕.
stepDesc.environment: Setup and requirements of the environment where it runs.
stepDesc.tools: The project's tools and automation strategy.
stepDesc.testData: How test data is created, protected and refreshed.
stepDesc.defects: How defects are logged, prioritised and closed.
stepDesc.roles: Who does what in the testing process.
stepDesc.schedule: Sprints and milestones of the test cycle. Click the start day and then the end day to create a sprint (Esc cancels). Select a sprint and drag its ends to change the dates, or edit them in its row. In «Milestone», click a day to add a milestone.
stepDesc.risks: Risks that can affect testing and how they are mitigated.
stepDesc.communication: How and when progress is reported.
stepDesc.closure: Conditions to meet before closing the cycle.
stepDesc.purpose: The test objectives the plan pursues and what it is for.
stepDesc.conclusion: Evaluation against objectives and exit criteria, open risks and the decision.
stepDesc.assumptions: What planning takes for granted and the limits the team cannot change (deadlines, people, rules). If an assumption stops holding, review the plan.
stepDesc.techniques: How test cases are designed (ISTQB CTFL v4, ch. 4): black-box, white-box, experience-based and collaboration-based.
stepDesc.estimation: How much effort and money it takes, and which technique gave the figure (CTFL v4 §5.1.4). In three-point estimation, E = (O + 4·M + P) / 6.
stepDesc.entry: When a cycle may start (entry criteria), when testing stops and what must happen to resume it.
stepDesc.metrics: What is measured and the objective it must reach. Pharos measures the catalog metrics; your own ones are judged by hand. Tick «Exit criterion» so they count when a cycle closes.
